forcedChoices.choice: tú for the generic «you» in the Cynic, Buddhist, Hindu, Taoist, and Confucian sayings
forcedChoices.reason: The sayings address one hearer in the manner of proverbs; ustedes is used where the English marks a plural (131:1.7, 131:1.8, 131:5.3, 131:7.2).

forcedChoices.choice: tú in the commandments and in the singular Hebrew addresses; ustedes in 131:2.3, 2.6 (Isaiah 30), 2.9, 2.10, 2.13
forcedChoices.reason: Follows the number that the context shows for each address.

forcedChoices.choice: tú when the speaker prays to God (131:4.2, 4.5, 5.4, 9.2)
forcedChoices.reason: Modern Spanish prayer uses tú; the English has no form of special respect.
Spanish forces a gender; the masculine is the generic form.

forcedChoices.choice: «que tiene siempre su asiento en el corazón»
forcedChoices.reason: Avoids a gender choice between «Dios» (masc.) and «la Gran Alma» (fem.) for «seated».

forcedChoices.choice: «un alma noble que se muestra amistosa ... serena ... generosa» (feminine)

forcedChoices.reason: Keeps open the two readings of «must» (inference or necessity).
Keeps open whether «its purpose» is the purpose of Heaven or of the soul.
«Lujurias» in the plural reads as only sexual sins; «apetitos» keeps the wider sense of strong desires.
